chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man proposes to a woman and consummates the marriage with her before she reaches nine years of age, they are separated and she is not permissible to him ever. This does not contradict what the report of Burayd contained from his saying: 'If he keeps her and does not divorce her, there is no penalty upon him,' because the correct interpretation is to understand it as: if the woman chooses to stay with him and he also chooses that, and she is satisfied with the blood money (diyah), it is permissible, and it is not permissible for him to have sexual relations with her in any state, according to what the later report contained, until we act upon all the reports.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries and consummates with a girl before she turns nine?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this report to resolve the apparent contradiction between the permanent prohibition (gharam) and the permissibility with compensation (diyah) by interpreting the latter as a case of mutual consent to retain the wife after paying the blood money. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of reconciling conflicting narrations through contextual interpretation rather than abrogation, specifically within the chapter on consummating marriage with a minor.
